macros.name: fancycenter
macros.doc: The command \fancycenter packs 3 header fields into a full-width header.

macros.name: fancyfootalign
macros.doc: The command \fancyfootalign allows you to fine-tune the vertical position of the footer with respect to the page bottom.

macros.name: fancyfootinit
macros.doc: \fancyheadinit and \fancyfootinit can be used to define initialisation code for the header and footer, respectively, and \fancyhfinit defines both of these.

macros.name: fancyhdrbox
macros.doc: The command \fancyhdrbox can be used to align multiline parts vertically and horizontally.

macros.name: fancyhdrbox
macros.doc: The command \fancyhdrbox can be used to align multiline parts vertically and horizontally.

macros.name: fancyhdrsettoheight
macros.doc: Sets ⟨lengthvar⟩ to the height of the ⟨header/footer⟩, which must be one of oddhead, evenhead, oddfoot or evenfoot.

macros.name: fancyheadinit
macros.doc: This macro can be used to define initialisation code that will be run before the construction of the header. It can for example set the color or the font, or change \headrulewidth or \headruleskip.

macros.name: fancyhf
macros.doc: There is also a more general command \fancyhf that you can use to combine the specifications for headers and footers.

macros.name: fancyhf
macros.doc: There is also a more general command \fancyhf that you can use to combine the specifications for headers and footers.

macros.name: fancyhfinit
macros.doc: \fancyheadinit and \fancyfootinit can be used to define initialisation code for the header and footer, respectively, and \fancyhfinit defines both of these.

macros.name: fancyhfoffset
macros.doc: Use \fancyhfoffset[place]{length} to offset one or more elements.

macros.name: fancypagestyle
macros.doc: This command lets you (re)define page styles for use in special situations.

macros.name: fancypagestyleassign
macros.doc: This command assigns page style ⟨ps2⟩ to ⟨ps1⟩. This causes ⟨ps1⟩ to be an exact copy of ⟨ps2⟩, but completely independent of ⟨ps2⟩.

macros.name: footrule
macros.doc: \headrule and \footrule are macros to completely redefine these lines.

macros.name: footruleskip
macros.doc: \headruleskip and \footruleskip are macros that define the distance between the lines and the header and footer text, respectively.

macros.name: footrulewidth
macros.doc: \headrulewidth and \footrulewidth are macros to define the thickness of a line under the header and above the footer.

macros.name: headruleskip

macros.name: headrulewidth
macros.doc: \headrulewidth and \footrulewidth are macros to define the thickness of a line under the header and above the footer.

macros.name: headwidth
macros.doc: The width of headers and footers is \headwidth, which by default equals the width of the text: \textwidth.

macros.name: ifbotfloat

arg.snippet: ifbotfloat{${1:value for bottom float}}{${2:value for other pages}}

macros.doc: The macros \iftopfloat, \ifbotfloat, \iffloatpage and \iffootnote are used to detect if there is a float on the top or the bottom of the page, or the page is a float page, or if there is a footnote at the bottom of the page.
